messages:
alex: Quick follow-up to the precision-profile RFC — we need a concrete plan for how Dedicated customers' runtime overrides interact with global FP8/INT8/4-bit rollouts. 2 questions: how do we validate per-customer quality, and what's the safe fallback surface?
maria: +1. We should avoid any global rollout that silently changes a customer's effective precision. Need a migration window + a visible audit.
jamal: proposal: treat per-customer overrides as higher precedence but require a validation badge before allowing INT8/4bit for a customer. badge = passed perf+quality tests on their production-ish prompt set.
sophia: agree on validation badge. Also we need a runtime flag that exposes "precision-negotiation" so apps can opt out. Example config: ```json
{ "precision_policy": "customer_override", "quality_escrow": "on", "negotiation": "opt-in" }
```
kevin: ops question — how do we avoid explosively high latency when a fallback triggers? e.g., switch from FP8 to fp32 fallback for a single request = bad. We should prefer model-variant fallback (e.g., fp8 -> int8 -> fp16) and rate-limit full-precision fallbacks.
alex: +1. Also want us to define metrics: per-customer degscore, rollout-impact, fallback-rate. These go into console so customers see the change.
maria: for the badge harness, can we reuse the existing eval infra? A simplified flow: 1) collect 1k weighted prompts 2) run candidate quantized model 3) compute degscore + latency delta 4) fail if degscore > threshold or latency delta > X%
jamal: operationally, also need a canary phase — allow 1% of traffic under new quant path with strict monitoring and automatic rollback if degscore spikes. ops-bot: canary-runner will create alerts when degscore change > 0.03 or fallback rate > 0.5%.
sophia: UX: expose a single toggle in Dedicated console "Allow low-bit optimizations" and a link to the validation badge + history. That reduces surprise.
kevin: corner case: customers with heavy long-context workloads — their SNR often collapses with aggressive quant. Suggest we add ctx-length-aware thresholds on the badge checks.
alex: actionable items: 1) jamal + maria to draft badge criteria and thresholds 2) eng-runtime to add precision-negotiation flag (opt-in/opt-out) 3) ops to wire canary-runner alerts 4) product to add console toggle + audit log. I'll collect and create a short RFC addendum.
maria: timeline idea: badge v0 in 2 weeks, console toggle + telemetry in 4 wks, rollout guardrails + canary policy in 6 wks.
jamal: i'll spin up a toy harness this week and post perf/nightly results here.
kevin: will prototype fallback hysteresis (avoid full-precision fallbacks for single-request blips).
sophia: tagging @eng-platform for routing policy implications. :eyes:
alex: thanks — ping me if any conflicts with dedicated customer SLAs.
